content: Have you ever wondered why you fall forward when a fast-moving bus suddenly stops? Or why a car doesn't move unless you push it, but once it is sliding on ice, it is hard to stop? In ancient India, scholars like Maharishi Kanada discussed the concept of 'Karma' (action/motion) in the Vaisheshika Sutras, exploring why things move. Today we will explore the invisible hand that rules our physical world: Force.
Imagine a smooth marble rolling on a perfectly smooth, endless glass floor. If nothing ever blocks it, will it eventually stop on its own, or will it roll forever? Why do you think so?

content.title: The Rolling Marble Experiment
content.description: Notice how the marble keeps rolling when there is zero friction.

content: Analogy: Think of a lazy Sunday morning. You don't want to get out of bed (state of rest) unless your mom pulls the blanket (external force). Similarly, once you are sprinting fast, you can't stop instantly on the finish line; your body wants to keep moving!

This tendency of objects to resist any change in their state of rest or motion is called Inertia (Jadatva). The word Inertia comes from the Latin root 'iners', meaning idle or lazy. This brings us to Newton's First Law of Motion: An object remains in a state of rest or of uniform motion in a straight line unless compelled to change that state by an applied unbalanced force.

question: What will happen to a book resting on a table if no unbalanced force acts on it?
options: It will fly into the air.

content: A common mistake is thinking that a continuous force is needed to keep an object moving in space. In reality, force is only needed to CHANGE the motion. Once moving in deep space, it keeps moving forever without any engine!
Reflection: Explain in your own words to your younger sibling: Why do we need to wear seatbelts in a car?

Connection: In the upcoming chapters, we will learn about Gravitation. Gravity is actually the ultimate unseen force that pulls everything together, connecting the inertia of a small apple falling from a tree to the motion of giant planets!

Mastery Challenge: Place a coin on a stiff playing card over an empty glass tumbler. Flick the card fast with your finger. If done right, the card flies away, but the coin drops straight into the glass due to its inertia of rest. Try it at home!
